A 68-year-old male patient, hospitalized 4 days ago for diverticulitis treatment, develops sudden
pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. His medical history includes stable chronic kidney disease
(serum creatinine 2.2 mg/dL; reference range 0.8–1.3). On examination, he is afebrile, with a blood
pressure of 108/83 mm Hg, heart rate of 115 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 21 breaths per
minute, and oxygen saturation of 85% on ambient air. He is alert, oriented, and mildly dyspneic. Lung
auscultation is clear bilaterally, but his left leg is swollen and tender. He is fully vaccinated against
Covid-19, and SARS-CoV-2 testing is negative. A portable chest X-ray reveals no opacities or
abnormalities in the heart or pleura. What is the next best step in managing this patient? Answer
Choices: (A) Administer supplemental oxygen and observe (B) Obtain a CT angiogram of the chest (C)
Initiate oral anticoagulation therapy immediately (D) Perform an echocardiogram to assess for right
heart strain (E) Perform a lower extremity Doppler ultrasound (F) Obtain a ventilation-perfusion scan of
the lungs (G) Order a D-dimer test to rule out pulmonary embolism (H) Administer thrombolytic therapy
immediately without further testing (I) Obtain an arterial blood gas analysis (J) Administer intravenous
heparin
 A. Perform a lower extremity Doppler ultrasound

B. Administer intravenous heparin
C. Initiate oral anticoagulation therapy immediately
D. Administer supplemental oxygen and observe
E. Order a D-dimer test to rule out pulmonary embolism
F. Obtain an arterial blood gas analysis
G. Obtain a CT angiogram of the chest
H. Obtain a ventilation-perfusion scan of the lungs
I. Administer thrombolytic therapy immediately without further testing
J. Perform an echocardiogram to assess for right heart strain
